_doc: The master grid of the iso village (L0-T03, replanned in FIN-DIS, docs/designs/village-loop/disposition-plan.md), read by components/village/iso/isoLayout.ts and scripts/iso/layout_preview.py. `sol` and `paliers` are rows, one per gy (row 0 = gy 0), one character per gx. `sol` uses `legende`; a building's plot is grass (`.`), its footprint is `emprise` in constants/isoSpec.json, its corner (smallest gx, smallest gy) is in `batiments`. One footprint cell is not grass: castle_wall's middle cell [17, 10] is the grand-route under its gate. `paliers` is the village tier (1-9, then a = 10, b = 11, c = 12) at which a cell joins the island, `-` for a cell never on it. It was generated: the tier of a cell = min(a metric, the target of the plot it is part of or borders, or of that plot's shadow or path to the campfire), then a pass that lifts a stray path cell, or lowers the cells joining it, so the path is one piece at every tier, then no hole. The metric is max(|dx|, |dy|) + min(|dx|, |dy|) / 2 around [11.5, 10], in steps of 1.25 cells. The targets are the plan's: camp and hall socle 1; farm, forge, archery and well 2; quarry and mill 3; mystic edge and fountain 4; armory, barn and the south wall's middle 5; gatehouse, watchtower, observatory and the east wall 6; the wall's west corner and the fields 7; high road, lair and the wall's east corner 8; arena 9; the country 10 to 12. So the island grows in lobes along the districts, and never recedes. A building can stand before its plot's tier (nothing in db/village.ts ties a building to the village tier): isoLayout.ts reveals its plot and its path then. Shadows fall toward +gx and -gy (screen right), so every building and every decor (heights.json `decors`) keeps its right and upper neighbours at the distance __tests__/iso-layout.test.ts measures, with the exceptions written there. The plan: the hall of heroes heads the square, the campfire [12, 11] on its screen axis, tent, dummy, fountain and well round it. Four ways into the square: the grand-route from the east through the gatehouse (row gy 10), the bridge over the river to the west (same row), the south gate (gx 12) and the edge to the north (gx 11); a wall walk runs inside the south wall (row gy 15). Farmers top left along the river (farm, barn, mill, well, fields), the military right toward the grand-route (dummy, armory, archery, gatehouse, watchtower), crafts at the square's corner and behind the hall (forge, quarry), the mystic edge at the back (grove, wizard tower; the observatory left it for [3, 12]), the monuments on the rim (arena outside the south wall, lair in the back rocks, high road on the road). The observatory stands at [3, 12], the corner of the farmers' lane in the open, and the mill behind the quarry at [7, 0] (iteration 3, Guillaume: the observatory was too hidden at [7, 1], between the quarry, the wizard tower and the forest; nothing else fits its shadow there). The mill's sails clear the quarry at [7, 0] but not at [7, 1] or [6, 1]; its front path is the cell [8, 2]. `rempart` is castle_wall's wall sections, one cell each, outside its footprint: drawn at its stage, on cells already on the island; a tap on one opens castle_wall. `champs` is the plan's fields, [gx, gy, w, h] in cells, drawn by components/village/iso/champs.ts once all their cells are on the island.

lieux._doc: Named places of the small lives (L5-AUD I6): the fireflies' patch of ground, the cells [from, to) in gx and gy, and the rat's run along one row, from gx0 to gx1 in the row gy, drawn `decalage` cells below the row's middle. The rat's cells are the whole cells of the run.

toits._doc: Where a crow perches on a roof (L5-T10), by painted stage `<code>_<stade>`: a point of the ridge's top edge, in sprite px (origin top left), read by eye on the painted sprite. A stage with no entry has no crow. A repainted sprite needs its point read again: __tests__/iso-corbeaux.test.tsx checks that each point sits on the sprite's own mask.
